modelResponse.episodeSummary: Marcus J. Okafor, Atrial Fibrillation with pre-excitation (WPW), critical severity, hemodynamically unstable (BP 82/48).
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Beat-to-beat QRS width and morphology variation; delta waves visible in wider beats
modelResponse.mechanism: Atrial fibrillation impulses are conducted to the ventricles via an accessory pathway that bypasses the AV node, allowing for extremely rapid ventricular rates due to the shorter refractory period of the accessory pathway compared to the AV node.
contributingFactors: Presence of an accessory conduction pathway

rejectedAlternatives.why: Variable QRS width (120-200ms) and visible delta waves indicate pre-excitation, which is not present in standard AFib.
Rhythm is 'irregularly irregular' and shows variable QRS morphology/width, whereas VT is typically regular and monomorphic or polymorphic without the specific delta wave characteristics of WPW.

recommendedActions: Immediate synchronized electrical cardioversion (Patient is hemodynamically unstable: BP 82/48, near-syncopal).

WITHHOLD AV nodal blocking agents (e.g., Beta-blockers, Calcium channel blockers, Digoxin) as these can paradoxically increase conduction through the accessory pathway and precipitate ventricular fibrillation.
